Export fitted MFRM tables to CSV files

Source: R/api-plotting.R
export_mfrm_tables.Rd

Writes tidy CSV files suitable for import into spreadsheet software or further analysis in other tools. This is the CSV-only route from a fitted model. It does not run diagnostics, save a complete R object, or create a replay script. Use export_mfrm_results() to archive an existing results object and reload it without refitting, or export_mfrm_bundle() for a fit-level collection with an optional refitting script. In 0.2.4 this replaces export_mfrm(); arguments, CSV filenames and the returned file table are unchanged. Enriched facet CSVs now also retain the diagnostic availability and uncertainty fields.

Usage

export_mfrm_tables(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  output_dir = ".",
  prefix = "mfrm",
  tables = c("person", "facets", "summary", "steps", "measures"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  acknowledge_sensitive = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm.

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm. When provided, enriches facet estimates with SE, fit statistics, their calculation/availability fields and reasons, and writes the full measures table. Must belong to the same fit; mismatched or outdated diagnostics are rejected before creating files.

output_dir

Directory for CSV files. Created if it does not exist.

prefix

Filename prefix (default "mfrm").

tables

Character vector of tables to export. Any subset of "person", "facets", "summary", "steps", "measures". Default exports all available tables.

overwrite

If FALSE (default), refuse to overwrite existing files.

acknowledge_sensitive

Logical; set to TRUE only after acknowledging that these tables can contain direct person identifiers, person-level estimates, and original facet labels. This suppresses the privacy warning; it does not deidentify any file.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame listing written files, their paths, and explicit privacy/data-handling metadata. Deidentified and ShareableWithoutReview are always FALSE.

Exported files

{prefix}_person_estimates.csv

Person ID, Estimate, SD.

{prefix}_facet_estimates.csv

Facet, Level, Estimate, and optionally SE, Infit, Outfit, PTMEA and their qualification fields when diagnostics are supplied.

{prefix}_fit_summary.csv

One-row model summary.

{prefix}_step_parameters.csv

Step/threshold parameters.

{prefix}_measures.csv

Full measures table (requires diagnostics).

Interpreting output

The returned data.frame tells you exactly which files were written and where. This is convenient for scripted pipelines where the output directory is created on the fly. The files are analysis tables, not a deidentified sharing package; review each file under the applicable data-handling policy before sharing it. In enriched facet tables, read SE_Method, SEUse, CIUse, InferenceReady and SupportsFormalInference with the SE. Read FitStatus and FitReason with Infit/Outfit. A finite value does not imply valid formal inference. These columns preserve the matching diagnostics' qualifications; the export does not compute a new SE or confidence interval. Missing fields in an older diagnostic result are not filled with assumed approval.

Typical workflow

  1. Fit a model with fit_mfrm().

  2. Optionally compute diagnostics with diagnose_mfrm() when you want enriched facet or measures exports.

  3. Call export_mfrm_tables(...) and inspect the returned Path column.

See also

fit_mfrm, diagnose_mfrm, as.data.frame.mfrm_fit, export_mfrm_results(), export_mfrm_bundle(), mfrmr_compatibility_layer

Examples

library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Use the diagnostics saved with this fit
diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics

# Use a new temporary folder for this example; choose a permanent one for your work
output_dir <- tempfile("mfrmr-tables-")
files <- export_mfrm_tables(
  fit,
  diagnostics = diagnostics,
  output_dir = output_dir,
  acknowledge_sensitive = TRUE # Synthetic data; exported tables retain person IDs
)

# Preview filenames; full paths remain in files$Path
data.frame(Table = files$Table, File = basename(files$Path))
#>      Table                      File
#> 1   person mfrm_person_estimates.csv
#> 2   facets  mfrm_facet_estimates.csv
#> 3  summary      mfrm_fit_summary.csv
#> 4    steps  mfrm_step_parameters.csv
#> 5 measures         mfrm_measures.csv
# Open a path from files$Path in a spreadsheet app or with read.csv()
